name: Pope Pius IX
role: Pope (1846–1878) and last sovereign of the Papal States
summary: Pius IX began his reign with reforms and an amnesty but after 1848 became a firm opponent of liberalism, nationalism and socialism. His Syllabus of Errors and Quanta Cura condemned religious liberty, state control of schools, civil marriage and divorce, and he held the Papal States' temporal power until Italy took Rome in 1870.

sources.title: The Syllabus of Errors (8 December 1864), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius IX
sources.usedFor: The 80 propositions he condemned on the Church, state, schools, marriage, religious liberty, non-intervention and modern liberalism.

sources.title: Quanta Cura (encyclical, 8 December 1864), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius IX
sources.usedFor: His condemnation of liberty of conscience and the press, popular will as supreme law, state control of schools and socialism; natural law in all hearts.

sources.title: Nostis et Nobiscum (encyclical, 8 December 1849), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius IX
sources.usedFor: His condemnation of socialism and communism, defence of property, natural inequality, obedience to authority, and family order.

sources.title: Pius IX, Encyclopaedia Britannica
sources.author: Britannica
sources.usedFor: The record: the 1848 constitution, flight and unconditional restoration in 1850, no constitutional government afterwards, hostility to Italian national sentiment, refusal of the 1870 settlement.

sources.title: Respicientes ea (encyclical on the seizure of the Papal States, 1 November 1870), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius IX
sources.usedFor: His rejection of the Piedmontese seizure of Rome and the plebiscites, defence of temporal power, his army.

sources.title: Ubi nos (encyclical on the Papal States and the Law of Guarantees, 15 May 1871), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius IX
sources.usedFor: His refusal of the guarantees, the claim that papal authority comes directly from God, necessity of civil rule.
